author: KONNER METZ
title: Officials shed light on outgoing, new Easton hospital properties - NewsBreak
text:
By KONNER METZ ,
13 hours ago
EASTON — The University of Maryland Shore Regional Health met with local officials this week, answering questions about Easton’s landmark hospital project, bed counts and more.
UM Shore Regional Health President and CEO Ken Kozel and Director of External Affairs Lara Wilson spoke to the Easton Town Council on Monday and the Talbot County Council on Tuesday. At each meeting they touched on the outgoing Easton medical center on South Washington Street and the 385,000-square-foot replacement on Longwoods Road, which is expected to be complete in mid-to-late 2028.
Kozel addressed head-on the question of why Shore Regional Health is building a new hospital without a major increase in the number of patient beds.
The new site will have 122 licensed inpatient beds, nearly even with the current 118. But 25 dedicated observation beds will be added.
“It’s going to give us so much more flexibility on how we care for our patients,” Kozel said of the new site on Monday.
Shore Regional Health had to acquire a certificate of need from the Maryland Health Care Commission, and the number of beds allowed was included in that certificate.
“We pushed the envelope with the state to get to 147 beds, and they’ve agreed to that number,” Kozel said.
Town Council President Don Abbatiello asked if the number of employees would increase. Kozel said it would be “comparable” but a “little bit more” — somewhere in the 1,750 to 2,000 range.
Workforce challenges
Meanwhile, at the current hospital, Town Council members asked about some shifts they have noticed in the workforce. Ward 3’s David Montgomery said he understands hospitals are struggling to retain primary care physicians.
Kozel called it “incredibly challenging” and said the system has supplemented the shortage with nurse practitioners in the meantime.
Wilson said Shore Regional Health is working with the University of Maryland and other groups to bring more medical students to the area.
“Help get them involved and want to work in rural health care, and then hopefully in the future become established in the community,” Wilson said.
Outgoing hospital
While officials prepare to move into the new medical center, the future of the current hospital property hangs in the balance.
In October, Shore Regional Health began working with a broker, CBRE, to market the sale of the 13.49-acre property. Multi-million dollar bid proposals from developers are starting to come in.
Next month, officials will start considering the bids and later present recommendations to the University of Maryland Medical System Board of Directions, which has final say on the matter.
Communication among Easton officials and the hospital system about the property’s sale hasn’t been perfect , Mayor Megan Cook said last month. Town and county leaders want to be involved in the process given that the hospital property is one of the largest downtown redevelopment opportunities in decades.
Kozel, Cook and Talbot County Council President Chuck Callahan have made it a priority to meet regularly to improve communication. And Cook said on Monday that the town wants to host community meetings this spring to gather feedback on what people want to see built at the site.
“He’s got an aggressive timeline,” Cook said of Kozel. “We’re looking to match that. We also think it would only benefit potential developers to understand what the community interests are in that property.”
Ward 1 Councilmember Maureen Curry said with bid proposals already coming in, it seems the hospital and town are “behind the 8-ball” and need to catch up. The Rev. Elmer Davis, who represents the 4th Ward where the current hospital is located, asked for further town involvement in the process.
“It should be a deeper consultation with the mayor and the council as a part of it,” Davis said.
